Cats of San Bernardino was started by Jaina and Ivy Spagis when they moved to San Bernardino in 2016
from Los Angeles. They were shocked that San Bernardino did not offer free spay and neuter
services like LA and realized that the feral situation in their new neighborhood was out of
control. They began trapping and spaying/neutering feral cats at their own expense, but soon
realized the problem was too big to tackle on their own.

They have converted their home into an animal sanctuary, providing space for kittens and their
mommas waiting for adoption, rehabilitation areas for recovering injured cats, play areas for
healthy cats. With the help of foster families in the city of San
Bernardino they have as many as 50 cats in their care at one time.Their dream is to one day
have a large property/facility which will help save thousands of more lives. This new property
would have catios, feral enclosures, a medical room, nursery, rehabilitation area, and adoption
center.

Named after a rescued horse saved nearly 30 years ago, Friends of Lackota Animal Sanctuary was founded to give animals a second chance at life. The sanctuary began when a young boy refused to let Lackota go to slaughter—working hard to save him and, in the process, finding a lifelong purpose.

Located in Northern Colorado, we specialize in rescuing horses and donkeys from the slaughter pipeline, but no animal is turned away if we can provide proper care. Many arrive from kill pens or auctions, often neglected, afraid, and broken. Here, they receive love, rehabilitation, and safety—whether they find a forever home or remain at the sanctuary.

Our mission is simple: help animals beat the odds and live the life they deserve.

Since 2008, we have been dedicated to helping neglected, abandoned, and mistreated dogs and cats in need of loving homes. We started as a small group of animal lovers working out of a garage until Nathan “Nate” Benderson, a local developer with an affinity for animals, caught wind of the group and joined. Nate provided the necessary vision and leadership to establish what is now known as Nate’s Honor Animal Rescue.

Today, together with a staff of caring volunteers and an incredibly supportive community, we save thousands of homeless and at-risk animals each year at our eight-acre, no-kill shelter and adoption facility on Lorraine Road.

As a 501(c)(3) non-profit animal rescue organization, we are proud to provide a place where homeless cats and dogs can receive the love and care they deserve while they wait to be welcomed into their forever homes.

The day-to-day operation of Ratlum Mountain Animal Rescue is handled by Christine & Ahren Paulson, a husband-and-wife team.  The Paulson's spent over a decade volunteering for other charities, rescuing, fostering & rehabilitating domestic animals (dogs and cats), in addition to serving on the Board of Directors. In 2017, Ahren & Christine decided to broaden the scope of their rescue activities by learning about wildlife rehabilitation & earning their Wildlife Custodian Appointments from the Connecticut DEEP. In early 2020, they established their own non-profit charity, Ratlum Mountain Animal Rescue Inc.

Christine & Ahren continue to work full-time day jobs, while volunteering and running the charity in the remainder of their time. They invite everyone to join them on this journey
